sections.h2: What is the Newaygo County register's address and schedule?
sections.html:
Look for the red-roofed Administration Building in downtown White Cloud, across the street from the post office. The register works from 1087 Newell Street (mail to box 885, ZIP 49349), answers at 231-689-7246 and keeps a fax line at 231-689-7271. Doors are open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday.

White Cloud became the seat of a county created in 1840 and organized in 1851. Deed records are indexed back to 1910, and the books themselves reach 1840, so an old family parcel often has a paper trail worth pulling before a sale. The office takes deeds, mortgages, land contracts, trusts and other papers about real property. It supplies no abstracts, forms or notary service, and it cannot tell you when a house was built because it handles land records only.

sections.h2: How does paper or electronic recording work in Newaygo County?
sections.html:
Photocopies and faxes are turned away. Only an original with live signatures is recorded, and a self-addressed stamped envelope gets the recorded paper back to you. Fees are collected on the spot and cannot be billed. You can pay with cash, check, debit or credit, though cards add a $3.50 charge on $100 or less and 3.5% above that.

E-recording follows the Michigan eRecording Standards that took effect January 1, 2014. The county handles e-filed documents from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, takes ACH payment and warns that the filing vendor may bill extra. Providers named on the page are CSC, ePN, Indecomm and Simplifile.

  • Left out of e-recording: court documents, death certificates, sheriff's deeds and surveys.
  • On paper, a court document or death certificate must be certified, since a plain true copy is refused.
  • A sheriff's deed goes on record within 20 days of the sale, so call the sheriff's office for sale details before bringing it in.

sections.h2: How is Newaygo County transfer tax worked out?
sections.html:
The county's own examples show the arithmetic. Shorthand on the page is $1.10 per $1,000 for the county and $7.50 per $1,000 for the state, applied after a price is rounded up to the next $500.

Newaygo County transfer tax examples (first two rows from the register's FAQ; third row computed with the same rates on the Census median home value, 2020-2024)
Price usedStateCountyTotal
$100,000$750.00$110.00$860.00
$100,000.01, treated as $100,500$753.75$110.55$864.30
$186,700, treated as $187,000$1,402.50$205.70$1,608.20

The grantor pays. A deed has to state total consideration, with any exemption written beside it, or both taxes are collected. Exchanges are taxed on the actual value of each parcel, and land lying in two counties gets a price split with tax paid to each. Stamps are bought only where the parcel is located, and filing a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit costs nothing.

sections.h2: What can a free search of the Newaygo County records show?
sections.html:
Grantor and grantee name searches cost nothing, and you can use the books yourself even though staff will not run searches for you. A tract index search starts from a legal description, which the county equalization department or your township can supply. A parcel number works too.

Everything recorded is public, so a buyer's title agent will see your deed, any mortgage discharge and any recorded survey. The register has a survey of your lot only if someone recorded one, and it knows lot dimensions only for recorded subdivisions and site condominiums. A deed describes the land, not the buildings on it. A new street address comes from the equalization department, not this office.

A fraud alert signup page on the county site suits owners of land they seldom visit.

sections.h2: What does the Newaygo County housing market look like?
sections.html:
West Michigan's Newaygo County covers 862 square miles, 813 of them land, with more than 230 natural lakes, 350 miles of rivers and streams and three big dams, Croton, Hardy and Newaygo. Over half the county lies within the Manistee National Forest, and the county operates parks, including a marina at Hardy Dam.

Census figures put the 2020 population at 49,978 and the July 2025 estimate at 51,622, up 3.3%. Owners occupy 86.5% of homes in a stock of 25,455 units. The typical owner-occupied home was worth $186,700 in 2020 to 2024, the median renter paid $904 and the median household earned $63,304. People spend an average 30.6 minutes commuting, and 111 building permits were issued in 2025.

Three towns anchor the map. Fremont, a city of 4,516, is home to Gerber and holds the National Baby Food Festival each July. Newaygo, population 2,471, sits on the Muskegon River, which once floated logs to Muskegon mills. White Cloud has 1,479 residents, lies on the White River and is a recognized Trail Town on the North Country Trail. The Newaygo County Regional Educational Service Agency in Fremont serves the public districts.

  • Tourism leads the economy, followed by farming and small manufacturing.
  • The register keeps plat books, which matter for lake lots in platted subdivisions.
  • Confirm the township before advertising a lake property, because the township assessor holds the tax record.

sections.h2: Which Newaygo County features do buyers ask about?
sections.html:
Summer cottage residents are common here, and anglers come for steelhead in spring and salmon in fall. Camping, hunting, cross-country skiing, cycling, birding and ORV riding fill the Manistee National Forest, so a listing that sits near public land should say so. Hardy Dam, completed early in the twentieth century, is the largest earthen dam east of the Mississippi, and the reservoirs behind the dams shape many shoreline sales.

Jobs help explain demand. Gerber employs about 1,300 people, according to the county's Wikipedia entry, and in White Cloud the county government, the public schools and North American Refractories are named as major employers. A feed mill that opened in the White Cloud Industrial Park in 2018, plus an airport with a 2,917-foot runway, adds to a small but active commercial base.

Fremont's history gives a sense of the area's age. Settlers arrived in 1855, Dutch families followed in the 1870s, and a forest fire in 1871 did heavy damage to the lumber mills. A seller with an old parcel near Fremont or Newaygo may find early plats and deeds in the register's books, which reach back to 1840.

sections.h2: What changes for taxes once a Newaygo County house sells?
sections.html:
Expect the buyer's taxable value to rise. Michigan resets it at the next assessment to state equalized value, half of true cash value, and the buyer has 45 days to notify the assessor. Close relatives who keep a residence non-commercial are excepted.

Ask the Newaygo County treasurer for a tax statement, and for the certification that has to be stamped before a warranty deed can be recorded.

faqs.q: When does the Newaygo County register of deeds close for the day?
faqs.a: The counter is open until 5 p.m. on weekdays. E-recorded documents are processed between 8:00 a.m. and 4:30 p.m., so a late file waits for the next business day.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax on a $100,000 house in this county?
faqs.a: $860.00, composed of $750.00 for the state and $110.00 for the county. The seller pays it, and any price is rounded up to the next $500 first.

faqs.q: Is there a charge for paying by card at the counter?
faqs.a: Yes: $3.50 on payments up to $100, and 3.5% of the payment above that. Cash and check carry no surcharge, and recording fees cannot be billed.

faqs.q: Can a sheriff's deed or death certificate be e-recorded here?
faqs.a: No. The e-recording rules exclude court documents, death certificates, sheriff's deeds and surveys, so those arrive on paper, certified where required.

faqs.q: Will the register record a photocopy of my signed deed?
faqs.a: No. Only originals with live signatures are accepted, and a court document needs the court's certification.
